Actor.description: The actor of a session or an event.

ActorKind.description: Whether the actor is a person or a program acting on its own.

oneOf.description: A person at a terminal or an editor.

ActorName.description:
What the actor is called: a tool name such as `claude-code`, or a person's
handle. Never a credential.

HostName.description: The name of a host a unit can live on.

Timestamp.description: A UTC instant, serialised as an RFC 3339 string.

UnitId.description: Identifies a `WorkUnit`. Stable for the life of the work, across machines.

description:
The single-writer claim on a unit.

Two clocks, and they answer different questions. `expires_at` is the absolute lapse
a transfer bundle carries from the host that made it. `refreshed_at` is when an
entry last touched the home, and the idle window is measured from it, so a person
working all day keeps the lock and a home nobody has entered since yesterday
releases it.

actor.description:
Who holds it. `None` for a row written before locks carried an actor: such a row
names a host and holds no actor, and the next entry rewrites it.

expires_at.description: When the claim lapses unless renewed.

host.description: The host that holds the write.

pid.description:
The process that took the hold. Recorded so a person can look. Nothing signals
it, and a lock is never expired because the process is gone.

refreshed_at.description: When an entry last touched the home.

taken_at.description: When the hold began, which a hand-off resets.

title: Lock
